summary: Chunk 4 (units 121-159), drug recipes for the pregnant woman. All 13 draft text_flags judged plausible and correctly kept as printed with the corrected form only in words (rāsnā, hiṅgu, kvātha, tvagghiṅgu, aśvagandhā, kālānusārya, icchayā, bhavanti, nidigdhikā, aikyam, pathyā, ṣaṇmāsād antra). Main findings: u137 Hindi/English did not mark the disputed or unidentified drugs (kākolī group, medā, mahāmedā, tagara, kṣīraśuklā), Hindi lacked hedges for mudgaparṇī/māṣaparṇī, Hindi supplied 'एक' for the unreadable oil measure, English supplied 'one'; u138 daivāepaghāta is only a split o-matra in the Devanagari (the real conjecture is mamo->mano); u132 has a plausible alternative payo (milk) beside prāyaḥ; u155 likelier parses as 'in the eighth month'; u149 'bark of the shoots' doubtful (shoots and bark of the milk-yielding trees); kālānusārya may be 'disputed' rather than 'unidentified'. Identifications otherwise sound and properly hedged. Human decisions: 128, 132, 135, 137 (kālānusārya), 138 (rājamātra), 149, 155. No regrouping needed.
glossary_suggestions: Devanagari ाे (ā-matra + e-matra) is the o-matra printed split; IAST renders it 'āe'. Treat 'āe' strings as ो (daivāepaghāta = daivopaghāta), not as damage; note once.
payasyā: always add the candidate in translations: English 'identity disputed; perhaps the Indian kudzu', Hindi 'सम्भवतः विदारीकन्द'.
Disputed or unidentified drug names in long recipe lists must be marked in both translations (kākolī, kṣīrakākolī, jīvaka, ṛṣabhaka, medā, mahāmedā, tagara, kṣīraśuklā).
Hindi mudgaparṇī = सम्भवतः जंगली मूँग; māṣaparṇī = सम्भवतः जंगली उड़द; śatapuṣpā = सोआ या सौंफ (विवादित); utpala = सम्भवतः नीलकमल; bṛhatī-dvaya = सम्भवतः बड़ी और छोटी कटेरी; kapittha = कैथ.
pañcakolaka = usually pippalī, pippalīmūla, cavya, citraka, śuṇṭhī (state once, hedge 'usually', the text does not name them).
kālānusārya: consider 'disputed' (tagara-type or black sārivā) instead of 'unidentified'.
Time compounds in -aha (trirātra, saptāha, daśāha): gram 'acc. sg. (duration)' without gender.
vṛkṣadanī printed for vṛkṣādanī: read as printed, note only.

Open: u132 prayo = prāyaḥ or payo (milk); u155 'māse tathā aṣṭame' = 'in the eighth month, likewise'; u149 kṣīri-śuṅga-tvacaḥ as dvandva (shoots and bark of milk trees); amaradāru/suradāru/devadāru all deodar synonyms, keep hedges consistent.
